title: Collateral challenges to jurisdiction
summary: A collateral challenge contests a judgment’s authority in a later proceeding rather than through ordinary review in the original action. Personal-jurisdiction choices can affect whether such a challenge remains open.
notes: A jurisdictional defect does not imply that every final judgment can be challenged at any time by any party. The precise defect, earlier litigation, and procedural route matter.

sections.Meaning: A collateral challenge contests a judgment’s authority in a later proceeding rather than through ordinary review in the original action. Personal-jurisdiction choices can affect whether such a challenge remains open.
sections.How to work through the question: Distinguish default followed by resistance to enforcement from appearing and litigating the jurisdictional issue. Identify whether the party already had an opportunity and an adjudication of that issue, and consider the finality rules discussed in the reading.
